title: ArtifactBuildPlan — one physical realization of a logical version
description: Everything the BuildSpec deliberately excludes: which engines, at which exact revisions, in which envelope format, with which physical parameters. Its SHA-256 under artifact@1 is `artifact_plan_sha256`, which is also the single-flight key for a build attempt together with (tenant, index_version_id). Changing anything here changes the artifact and never the logical version.

format_version.description: Munarium artifact envelope version. Major versions are not assumed readable by older binaries; minor versions may add optional files only when a feature bit makes the behaviour explicit.

feature_bits.description: Sorted, deduplicated. A reader that does not recognise a REQUIRED feature refuses the artifact before opening any engine file.

engine_revision.description: The exact upstream revision: a pinned semver or an immutable git rev. A floating range or a branch name is not a revision and is refused.

vector.description: Null means the artifact has no vector leg, which is valid when the BuildSpec has no embedder. A plan must not declare a vector leg the spec cannot supply.

kind.description: Exact is the correctness oracle and the small-index fast path; approximate requires the recall gate against it.

range_map.description: Optional. Reserved in v1 so a later verified remote-range reader can fetch immutable blocks without a manifest-schema major bump. An artifact built without one remains whole-hydrate-only and can be rebuilt as a new physical artifact of the same logical version.

shaper.description: How the physical settings above were CHOSEN. Recording the decision inputs is what makes a build policy auditable rather than a story about what someone probably ran; settings must never be chosen from transient runtime load, and a plan that cannot say why it picked approximate vectors cannot be reviewed.
